newsitem.title: GREECE: Expected money squeeze pulls Greek short rates up.
newsitem.headline: Expected money squeeze pulls Greek short rates up.

text.p: Expectations of a liquidity shortage early next week drove short depos and forex forwards higher by 20 to 25 basis points in late trade, dealers said.
"Shorts are up 20 to 25 basis points as the market braces for a liquidity shortage early next week," said a money trader at a foreign bank. "Long tenors are holding Thursday afternoon levels."
The central bank surprised the market by keeping its intervention overnight bid intact at 12.40 percent. Market players had said they expected the Bank to slash its intervention bid this week.
Greece will issue three-, six- and 12-month T-bills at unchanged yields of 11.90, 12.10 and 12.70 percent respectively on Monday, September 30.
The finance ministry privately placed 7-year FRNs at par worth 830 billion drachmas carrying an annual coupon of 14.20 percent with some local state and private banks.

It also privately placed an unspecified amount of T-bills with at least one state bank, dealers said. The bank received an enhanced commission for the T-bill private placement, which market talk estimated at close to 300 billion drachmas.
The mark was quoted at 158.11/21 drachmas from Friday's 158.000 fix, the dollar at 240.65/75 drachmas from 240.740 and the Ecu at 301.40/50 from 301.330 drachmas.
"The Ecu firmed slightly versus the drachma but nothing interesting happened at the fixing," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank.
